resources.string: Android blocks the accessibility toggle for apps installed from a downloaded APK file. This is an OS security policy, not a RikkaMinis bug — nothing is wrong with your install. Allowing restricted settings only re-enables the toggle; it grants nothing on its own, and you still choose whether to turn the service on.
One tap — clears the flag without leaving RikkaMinis
Failed — use the manual steps below
App info → ⋮ menu (top right) → Allow restricted settings
RikkaMinis lost its accessibility permission — this happens after the app is force-stopped. Shizuku is available, so it can be restored right now without opening Settings.
RikkaMinis lost its accessibility permission — this happens after the app is force-stopped. Re-enable RikkaMinis under Settings → Accessibility to continue.
Android removes the accessibility grant whenever an app is force-stopped, and does not restore it automatically. Shizuku can write it back directly.
Android removes the accessibility grant whenever an app is force-stopped, and does not restore it automatically. Install and authorize Shizuku to repair this in one tap in future.
Repair failed — try enabling it in Settings
The permission was revoked, likely by a force-stop
